item.title: Installing
item.description:
This page gets devvm installed and checked on your machine. Upgrading and uninstalling covers what comes later.

Installing devvm

Run the command for your system:

# Install devvm, and Lima with it
brew trust --formula devvmhq/tap/devvm
brew install devvmhq/tap/devvm

The install script in the Linux tab also works on macOS.

# Install devvm and what it needs
curl -fsSL https://github.com/devvmhq/devvm/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash

The script asks before it installs Lima, QEMU or access to /dev/kvm.

Install devvm one way, with Homebrew or with the install script, but not both (one devvm). The install script needs curl, tar, and sha256sum or shasum, it never needs sudo for devvm itself, and it checks the download’s checksum and signature before it installs anything (Installing and updating). To check the script itself against devvm’s release key before you run it, follow checking the install script. It takes options after bash -s --, as in curl -fsSL … | bash -s -- --yes:

Option What it does
--yes answer yes to every question
--version 0.1.0, or DEVVM_VERSION=0.1.0 install that release
--no-deps install devvm only
--force install even when Homebrew installed devvm, which leaves you with two copies
DEVVM_PREFIX=/some/dir install under that folder instead of ~/.local

Requirements

devvm runs its VMs on Lima, its default backend. It’s tested on Apple silicon Macs and on Linux on both arm64 and x86_64, but not yet on Intel Macs (Known limits). The last column says whether the install script offers to install a requirement for you.

You need To check To get it The install script
macOS at Lima’s minimum, on arm64 or x86_64 sw_vers and uname -m doesn’t
8 GiB of memory and 4 CPUs, recommended sysctl hw.memsize hw.ncpu doesn’t
Lima at its minimum limactl --version brew install lima, or Lima’s install guide offers it: Homebrew’s when you have Homebrew, otherwise Lima’s latest release into ~/.local
OpenSSH 8.7 or newer, for ssh and editors by name (details) ssh -V macOS 13’s has it doesn’t
Docker Desktop, only for --from with an image only Docker has docker version Docker Desktop doesn’t
You need To check To get it The install script
Linux on arm64 or x86_64 uname -m doesn’t
8 GiB of memory and 4 CPUs, recommended free -g and nproc doesn’t
Lima at its minimum limactl --version brew install lima, or Lima’s install guide offers it: Homebrew’s when you have Homebrew, otherwise Lima’s latest release into ~/.local
QEMU qemu-img --version your package manager: apt, dnf, pacman or zypper offers it, with sudo
Access to /dev/kvm ls -l /dev/kvm sudo usermod -aG kvm $USER, then log out and back in offers it, with sudo
OpenSSH 8.7 or newer, for ssh and editors by name (details) ssh -V Ubuntu 22.04’s has it doesn’t
Docker’s engine, only for --from with an image only Docker has docker version Docker’s engine doesn’t
  • A smaller machine works too. devvm gives base fewer CPUs and less memory there (size and ports).
  • Your first VM needs 8 GiB of free disk space, for the base image, the VM’s own image and the shared tools (free space).
  • Everything else goes inside the VMs, including the toolchains, the coding agents and Docker for your projects (docker layer), so you don’t install any of the supported coding agents on this machine (devvm’s agent store).
  • Linux hosts have a few limits, such as .git protection that needs a kernel which lets devvm use a user namespace, which Ubuntu 23.10 and newer don’t by default (Known limits).

Checking what devvm needs

Run devvm doctor:

devvm doctor

It lists everything that devvm’s backend, Lima, needs and doesn’t have, each with what to do, then its warnings, such as a machine with less than the recommended memory, and it fails only when something is missing. devvm never installs anything on this machine itself, and every command that needs the backend checks it first and stops at the first thing that’s missing. What devvm doctor checks lists each check and warning.

When devvm doctor finds nothing missing, you’re ready for your first VM. Before you make it, read staying safe, which lists the habits that close most of what devvm leaves open.

item.title: Your first VM
item.description:
This page assumes you’ve installed devvm and that devvm doctor finds nothing missing.

Making the VM

  1. Run devvm in a project folder.

    cd ~/some-project
devvm

  2. Answer the first-run questions. The first time, devvm asks for the CPUs and memory new VMs get, the coding agents they get, and the optional extras the base image gets, such as oh-my-bash and fzf. These set devvm’s defaults for every new VM, and devvm setup changes them later (devvm setup).

  3. Check the summary. devvm shows what this folder’s new VM gets: the toolchains your folder’s files call for, the agents and layers you chose for new VMs, its size, its network tier and its ports.

    ==> This folder's new VM, devvm-some-project-71a99b1076d92c, gets:
 toolchain node, for package.json
 agent claude, from devvm setup
 layers: none
 size: 4 CPUs, 8 GiB of memory and a 100 GiB disk
 network tier: allowlist
 ports: all
Customize it? [y/N]

  4. Confirm, or customize it. Confirm to make the VM as shown, or customize it to choose its toolchains, coding agents, layers, network tier, ports and size first (what a new VM gets). Flags such as --agents claude choose a part beforehand, and devvm asks nothing when the flags choose everything.

    Tip

    Keep allowlist, the default, unless the VM needs more. The allowlist network tier limits the VM to the hosts you allow, and every tier keeps your secrets on your machine. When you don’t know yet which hosts the project needs, choose learn: the VM reaches any public host while it learns them, and devvm network lock then keeps the ones you choose on the allowlist tier (learning the hosts a VM needs).

  5. Wait for the base image. The first time, devvm builds it with the extras you chose, which takes a few minutes once, and later VMs start in seconds (images).

    ==> building image base (e9f517dddef1)
 a few minutes, and Ubuntu's cloud image to download the first time
 (details: ~/.local/share/devvm/logs/runs/20261024-090616-83541.log)
==> image base ready
==> creating devvm-some-project-71a99b1076d92c from base
==> starting devvm-some-project-71a99b1076d92c

Then devvm opens a shell in the VM at the same path, ~/some-project, with (devvm) at the start of the prompt.

Claude Code’s login

If the VM has Claude Code, log it in to your Claude account once. Run this in a terminal on this machine, not the VM’s shell, in the project folder:

devvm agent login claude

Open the address it shows in a browser, approve the login, and paste the code the browser shows. devvm keeps the login on this machine for every VM with Claude Code, and the VMs get only a placeholder (Claude Code login). If you already use an agent on this machine, devvm agent import copies its settings and logins into devvm’s agent store instead (devvm’s agent store).

Starting the agent

Start the agent in the VM’s shell, so it runs in the VM:

~/some-project $ devvm
(devvm) ~/some-project $ claude

Run the agent the VM has by its name, such as claude, which the supported agents table lists (running an agent).

What’s in the VM

  • Your project folder, read-write, so your editor and the VM share the same files. It’s the only folder of yours the VM sees, and its .git hooks and config are locked, except on a Linux host that can’t lock them, such as Ubuntu 23.10 and newer, where devvm only watches them (.git protection).
  • The toolchains, ready at once (toolchains).
  • Your git name and email, so commits made in the VM are yours.
  • Ports: a dev server on :5173 in the VM opens at localhost:5173 on your machine (ports).
  • sudo without a password, so apt install works as on any Ubuntu machine.

Working on a clone instead

To keep the VM out of your working tree and .git entirely, make it with its own clone of the repo:

devvm --clone # a VM with its own clone of your branches
git fetch devvm # later, on this machine: the VM's work as devvm/<branch>
git log -p main..devvm/main # review it before you merge it

Use it for an agent working unattended, a repo you don’t trust, or on a Linux host whose kernel doesn’t let devvm protect .git (working on a clone).

Coming back to it

The VM belongs to its folder, and its subfolders use it too (a subfolder):

devvm # a shell in this folder's VM, started if it's stopped
devvm tools # choose its toolchains and agents
devvm tools add claude # add Claude Code to this folder's VM
devvm code # open it in VS Code
devvm stop # stop it
devvm ls # list every VM
devvm rm # delete it after asking, saving its agents' history first

Everyday commands lists the rest, and managing VMs covers restarting, deleting and moving VMs. Before you let an agent loose in the VM, read staying safe.

item.title: Everyday commands
item.description:
This page lists devvm’s commands in the groups that devvm --help shows them in, and each row links to the page with the details. devvm COMMAND --help shows a command’s examples and flags, the command line covers what works the same in every command, and the CLI reference has every command with all its flags.

Your VM

devvm open a shell in this folder’s VM, at the same path, making the VM first with the toolchains, agents and layers you choose, or that --tools, --agents and --layers name (details)
devvm restart stop this folder’s VM, start it again and open a shell in it, for changes that apply only when it starts (details)
devvm stop stop this folder’s VM (details)
devvm update [--force] [--no-export] [--clean-home] move this folder’s VM to the newest shared tools, and when its image or its devcontainer.json has changed, make it again from the image’s new build and the file as it is now, keeping its home folder and settings, after asking, then open a shell in it (details)
devvm rm [--force] [--no-export] [--no-clone-check] delete this folder’s VM after asking, exporting its agents’ history first unless --no-export (details)
devvm rm VM [--force] [--no-export] [--no-clone-check] delete a VM whose folder is gone, by its name or ssh alias, after asking (details), or one whose folder is on a disk that isn’t connected, only after asking in a terminal (details)
devvm adopt use the VM made for an earlier folder at this path here (details), or the VM made for this folder before you moved or renamed it (details)
devvm adopt VM move a VM whose folder is gone to this folder, such as a copy of that folder on another disk, after asking (details)
devvm ls list the project VMs (details)
devvm code get this folder’s VM ready as devvm host does, then open its folder in VS Code over Remote-SSH (VS Code)
devvm desktop [--clipboard] [--no-open] serve this folder’s VM’s desktop on 127.0.0.1 with its password until Ctrl+C, and open it in Screen Sharing on macOS (details)
devvm host get this folder’s VM ready for ssh and editors, and show the host name they reach it by, such as devvm-website (details)
devvm history list the exports of agents’ history that devvm saved in ~/.local/share/devvm/exports (details)
devvm history export [FILE] save the history of this folder’s VM’s agents to FILE, or to a new .tar.gz in ~/.local/share/devvm/exports (details)
devvm history import [FILE] put the agents’ history in FILE, or in the newest export devvm saved for this folder, into this folder’s VM (details)
devvm paste [--json] [--send-file] send the image, the PDF, or the one copied file, after asking about a file, on this machine’s clipboard into this folder’s running VM’s paste folder, and copy its path there for your terminal’s paste shortcut (details)
devvm paste rm [--force] delete the files devvm paste left in this folder’s running VM, after asking (details)

In a folder without a VM of its own, each of these commands but devvm adopt uses the VM of the nearest folder with one that it’s inside, and says which VM that is. --here and --parent choose which VM a command uses (a subfolder).

These options are for a new VM, and only devvm takes them. A VM that exists ignores them with a warning (what a new VM gets).
--tools LIST|none the toolchains the VM gets, such as --tools node,python, in place of those the folder’s files call for (details)
--agents LIST|none the coding agents the VM gets, such as --agents claude,codex, in place of those devvm setup chose (details)
--layers LIST|none the layers the VM’s image gets, bottom first, such as --layers docker, in place of those devvm setup chose (details)
--network TIER create the VM on a network tier: open reaches anything this machine can, internet any public host, allowlist, the default, only the hosts you allow, and none only its agents’ and secrets’ hosts and its links
--clone create the VM with its own clone of the repo, or of each repo in a folder of repos, instead of mounting the folder (details)
--repos all|none|LIST with --clone in a folder of repos, the repos the VM gets a clone of, such as --repos frontend,backend, in place of the picker (details)
--no-git-protect create the VM without .git protection
--ssh-agent create the VM forwarding your SSH agent, so while you’re connected, anything in it can use your keys (details)
--unsafe-folder mount a folder that devvm refuses, such as one that is or holds your home folder (details)
--cpus N, --memory GiB, --disk GiB the VM’s size (details)
--ports all|none|LIST which ports the VM forwards (details)
--from IMAGE start its base from a container image, such as node:24, instead of Ubuntu’s cloud image (details)
--no-devcontainer create the VM without reading the folder’s devcontainer.json, which otherwise describes the VM as far as devvm supports it, with the options you give taking priority (details)

Working on a clone

devvm --clone make this folder’s VM with its own clone of the repo, copy your branches into it and open a shell in the clone (details)
git fetch devvm on this machine, fetch the VM’s work as devvm/<branch>, to review before you merge it (details)
devvm clone fetch [--json] fetch the VM’s work into every repo it has a clone of, and list the new or moved branches, each with its repos (details)
devvm clone add PATH copy one more repo of a folder of repos into the VM, at the same path (details)
devvm rm delete the VM, first offering to keep the work you haven’t fetched as saved/devvm/<branch> branches (details)
devvm clone on|off make an existing VM again with its own clone of the repo, or with the folder mounted once devvm has offered to keep the clone’s work as devvm rm does (details)

Change your VM

devvm tools in a terminal, choose this folder’s VM’s toolchains and agents in a list, then open a shell in it, and otherwise show its shared tools, each with its version and any newer one (details)
devvm tools add TOOL... add shared tools to this folder’s VM, such as devvm tools add python claude, then open a shell in it (details)
devvm tools rm TOOL... take shared tools out of this folder’s VM, such as devvm tools rm python claude, then open a shell in it
devvm tools update move this folder’s VM to the newest shared tools, and only those, then open a shell in it (details)
devvm size [--cpus N] [--memory GiB] [--disk GiB] show or change this folder’s VM’s CPUs, memory and disk (details)
devvm size -g ... show or change the size new VMs get (details)
devvm mount-cache [none] show how this folder’s VM caches its project folder on a Linux host, none, which new VMs get, or Lima’s mmap, which can lose writes, or switch it to none from the VM’s next start (details)
devvm ports [all|none|LIST] show or change which ports this folder’s VM forwards to this machine’s localhost, even while it runs (details)
devvm ports add|rm LIST forward more ports, or stop forwarding some (details)
devvm ports -g ... show or change what new VMs forward (details)
devvm network [open|internet|learn|allowlist|none] show this folder’s VM’s tier, open, internet, internet (learning), allowlist, none or unenforced, and then its allowlist, file by file, or give it a tier: between the confined tiers at once, and into or out of open from its next start, offering to restart a running VM now, and with learn, internet while it learns the hosts it needs (details)
devvm network -g [open|internet|allowlist|none] show or change new VMs’ tier, which is allowlist until you change it (details)
devvm network lock [--all] [--none] choose which of the hosts this folder’s VM learned it keeps, add them to its own rules, and give it the allowlist tier (details)
devvm network allow|deny|rm RULE... [-g] add allow or deny rules to this folder’s VM’s own, or remove them, at once, and with -g, change yours for every VM (details)
devvm network allow|deny|rm RULE... --method METHODS --path PATH narrow those rules to some of a host’s requests, such as only GET and HEAD (details)
devvm network log [--follow] [-n N] [--blocked] show what this folder’s VM connected to and what its proxy blocked (details)
devvm network transparent [on|off] show whether this folder’s VM sends tools that ignore the proxy settings to its proxy by the names they look up, and where that comes from, or give the VM its own setting, from its next launch (details)
devvm ssh-agent [on|devvm|off] show this folder’s VM’s SSH agent forwarding, which is off, on for yours or devvm for devvm’s own, then the keys devvm’s own agent holds and those added to it, or change the forwarding from the VM’s next start (details)
devvm ssh-agent add KEY_FILE [--confirm] [--lifetime DURATION] load a key into devvm’s own agent, and load it again whenever a VM needs it (details)
devvm ssh-agent rm KEY_FILE take a key out of devvm’s own agent, so devvm doesn’t load it again (details)
devvm git-protect [on|off] show or change this folder’s VM’s .git protection, while it’s stopped (details)
devvm clone [on|off] [--force] [--no-export] [--clean-home] [--no-clone-check] [--repos LIST] show whether this folder’s VM has its own clone of the repo, or make it again with one, or with the folder mounted, keeping its home folder and settings, after asking, then open a shell in it (details)
devvm secret, devvm secret rm NAME list the secrets, whether each is saved and the VMs using it, or delete a saved one (details)
devvm secret set claude|github [--stdin] save your Claude Code token or GitHub token on this machine, so that VMs get a placeholder and their proxy puts the secret in (details)
devvm secret set NAME --host HOST --env VARIABLE save a secret of your own, such as an API key, which VMs that use it send only to its hosts (details)
devvm secret use|unuse NAME let this folder’s VM use a secret, or stop it, though a VM with Claude Code always uses claude (details)
devvm layer add LAYER... [--force] [--no-export] [--clean-home] make this folder’s VM again with more layers on top, keeping its home folder and settings, after asking, then open a shell in it (details)
devvm layer rm LAYER... [--force] [--no-export] [--clean-home] make this folder’s VM again without some of its layers, keeping its home folder and settings, after asking, then open a shell in it (details)

Links between VMs

devvm link list this folder’s VM’s links, each with its name, port, target VM and folder, the target’s status, and whether the link applies (details)
devvm link add TARGET PORT [--as NAME] link this folder’s VM to PORT of the VM that TARGET names, so programs in it reach the port as NAME:PORT and NAME.devvm.internal:PORT (details)
devvm link rm TARGET PORT remove one of this folder’s VM’s links (details)
devvm link publish [PORTS] show the ports this folder’s VM publishes, or offer PORTS to links from any of your other VMs (details)
devvm link unpublish PORTS stop offering ports to links (details)
devvm group show the group this folder’s VM is in, with each of its VMs, the name the others reach it by, its folder and the ports it publishes (details)
devvm group join NAME [--as NAME] put this folder’s VM in the group NAME, which its first VM makes, so each VM in the group reaches the ports the others publish (details)
devvm group leave take this folder’s VM out of its group, removing the links the group made (details)

Images

devvm images list the images, then the shared tool images (details)
devvm images rm IMAGE|KEY... delete images, by name or by the key devvm images shows (details)
devvm build IMAGE build an image and the images under it, unless they’re built, such as devvm build docker or devvm build foo+bar, where IMAGE is base or layers and never a shared tool (details)
devvm rebuild IMAGE build an image of base or layers again from its parent as it is, and delete the stale images no VM uses, while shared tools follow the tools lock instead (details)
devvm layer new NAME start a layer of your own, ~/.config/devvm/layers/NAME.sh, with its allowlist, NAME.policy (details)

devvm build, devvm rebuild and devvm images rm take --from IMAGE to work on a base made from that container image (details).

Disk space

devvm space show what devvm keeps on this machine, the disk each kind takes, and what frees it (details)
devvm gc delete the stale and unfinished images and the tool images no VM uses, after listing them, and never a VM (details)
devvm retention [KEY=VALUE...] show the retention settings, which say what devvm deletes on its own, or change them, with KEY=off turning one off (details)

This machine

devvm setup [--features LIST|none] [--agents LIST|none] [--layers LIST|none] choose base’s features and the coding agents and layers new VMs get, and in a terminal also new VMs’ size and network tier (details)
devvm agent import [AGENT...] copy the agents’ settings and logins from your home folder into devvm’s agent store, which every VM gets them from, never their history, asking before it replaces the store’s (details)
devvm agent login AGENT [--setup-token] [--device-code] [--api-key] log an agent in inside this folder’s VM, such as Claude Code to your Claude subscription, or get a Claude Code token with --setup-token (details), or log an agent in to ChatGPT there, in a browser on this machine or with a code, or save an API key, and keep the login in devvm’s agent store for every VM (details)
devvm agent save [AGENT...] copy the agents’ settings from this folder’s VM into devvm’s agent store, never their logins or history, after showing what changed and asking (details)
devvm doctor check what devvm needs on this machine and say how to get what’s missing (details)
devvm upgrade [--check] [--to VERSION] install devvm’s newest release the way you installed devvm, after asking, or with --check only say whether a newer one is out (details)
devvm completion SHELL print the shell completion script for bash, zsh or fish (details)
devvm limactl ARGS... run Lima’s limactl on the VMs and images in devvm’s own Lima home, not ~/.lima, for debugging, which starts VMs unconfined, whatever their tier (details)

devvm itself

devvm help [COMMAND] print the help for devvm or a command, as --help and -h do (details)
devvm --version print devvm’s version alone, as devvm version also does

The folders devvm keeps its state in and the environment variables it reads are in Settings and files.
